sentences.text: THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING, THIS DAY, K.S.MUDAGAL.J, DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT "Whether the compensation awarded to the claimant under the impugned award is just?" is the question involved in the case.
2. The appellant was the claimant and respondents were respondent Nos.1 and 2 before the Tribunal.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties will be referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the Tribunal.

3. On 30.01.2011 at 5.25 p.m. the claimant was working as cleaner in tipper lorry bearing registration No.KA.No.09-B-3344 and the said tipper lorry was deployed in road construction project near Dyapegowdana Doddi, Kanakapura Taluk.

At that time, when the driver of the tipper lorry was taking the said vehicle in reverse mode for spreading jelly powder on the road, the hydraulic machine attached to the said lorry hit the stomach portion of the claimant.
When he fell down the rear wheel of the tipper lorry ran over him causing him grievous injuries.
4. Regarding the accident one Prasanna Kumar filed complaint as per Ex.P2 against the driver of the tipper lorry.
Based on the said complaint, FIR Ex.P1 was registered against the driver of the tipper lorry for causing the accident by actionable negligence.
The driver of the lorry pleaded guilty of the offences.
At the relevant time respondent Nos.1 and 2 were the registered owner and insurer of the offending lorry.

5. The claimant filed MVC No.948/2012 against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.44,40,000/- alleging that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the tipper lorry causing him permanent physical disability.
He claimed that due to such accident he has suffered loss of future earnings etc., and respondents are liable to pay the damages.

6. The respondents contested the petition denying the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the tipper lorry, age, occupation, income of the deceased, the injuries suffered by him and the physical disability alleged by him.
They contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the claimant himself and they are not liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: To substantiate his claim, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and the doctors who treated him as CWs.1 to 3.
On his behalf Exs.P1 to P13 and Exs.C1 to C28 were marked.
The driver of the vehicle was examined as RW.1 and Ex.R1 was marked on their behalf.
8. The Tribunal on recording the evidence of the parties and hearing them by the impugned award held that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the tipper lorry.

The Tribunal relying on the evidence of CWs.1 to 3 the Doctors and the evidence of PW.1 the claimant held that due to the injuries suffered in the accident the claimant has suffered 20% permanent physical disability.
The Tribunal notionally assessed his income at Rs.4,500/- per month, his age at 26 years, applied 17 multiplier and assessed loss of future earning at Rs.1,83,600/-.

The Tribunal in all awarded the compensation of Rs.7,81,600/- on different heads as per the table below:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in Rs.
 1. Pain and Suffering 1,00,000/-
 2. Medical expenses and 4,00,000/-
 Attendant charges, Special  Diet, etc

3 . Loss of Amenities of life 60,000/-
 4. Loss of income during rest 18,000/-
 5. Future Medical Expenses for 20,000/-
 removal of implants  6. Loss of future earnings 1,83,600/-
The claimant challenges the said award on the ground that the compensation awarded on all the heads is on lower side.

Submissions of Smt. Shobha S. Bhavikatti, learned Counsel for the appellant:
10.
Having regard to the nature of the injuries and the period of hospitalisation, the compensation awarded on the head of pain and suffering is on the lower side.
The notional income and disability assessed are on the lower side.
The Tribunal was not justified in reducing the medical expenses on Rs.6,25,196/- to 4,00,000/- without any reason.
The Tribunal ought to have awarded the separate compensation on the head of attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance.

Submissions of Sri. B.Praddep, learned Counsel for respondent No.2/insurer:
11.
The compensation awarded on the head of pain and suffering is just one.
Since there was no proof of income, the Tribunal was justified in assessing the income at Rs.4,500/- per month.

Analysis:
12.
The finding with regard to the occurrence of the accident due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the lorry is not challenged.
The evidence on record shows that the claimant was treated as inpatient between 31.01.2011 to 01.04.2011 in Vikram Jeev hospital, Mysuru.
Thereafter, the petitioner was again treated as indoor patient in JSS Institute of Nephro Urology, Mysuru between 02.08.2011 to 15.08.2011.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Again he was treated as inpatient in JSS hospital, Mysuru between 16.01.2012 and 30.01.2012.
13. Ex.P8 the discharge summary issued by Vikram Jeev hospital, Mysuru and Ex.P6

The evidence of CW.1 the Orthopedic Surgeon shows that, the claimant suffered Pelvic fracture-anterior column, fracture of acetabulum left with bilateral superior and inferior pubic rami fracture, Lateral condyle avulsion fracture of right femur and soft tissue injury with fracture left foot.

15. Medical evidence further shows that the claimant had suffered Peno scrotal injury with urethral injury and exposed testis, for scrotal injuries he underwent suprapubic cystostomy with scrotal suturing on 31.01.2011 by the Urologist.
For his pelvic fracture he underwent emergency vascular repair (Bypass) with (L) pelvis fixation with fasciotomy on 31.01.2011 by the Plastic Surgeon and CW.1.
On 01.02.2011 additional fasciotomy was done by the Plastic Surgeon.
16. CW.1 the Orthopedic Surgeon who treated the claimant assessed the disability of right lower limb at 8.49% and left lower limb at 55.7%.
He assessed the disability to the whole body at 21.39%.
The Tribunal without assigning any reason reduced the same to 20% which was not justifiable one.
Having regard to the nature of injure, the medical evidence and nature of the employment of the claimant, it is just to consider the disability of the claimant at 22% to the whole body.
17. It was not disputed that at the relevant time claimant was working as cleaner in tipper lorry.
It is true that there was no proof of actual income.
His age at 26 year was not disputed.

Under such circumstances considering the said aspects, prevailing rate of wages and cost of living during 2011 the accident period, the Tribunal should have considered his notional income at Rs.6,500/- per Sri T N Srinivasa vs Sri H S Ramesh on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6276729/

sentences.text: The applicable multiplier is 17, therefore the compensation payable on the head of loss of future earning comes to (Rs.6,500 x 12 x 17 x 22/100)= Rs.2,91,720/-.
18. Claimant was admitted in the hospital for 88 days.

Having regard to the nature of his injuries,
period of the hospitalisation and the medical evidence, the Tribunal ought to have awarded loss of income during laid up period for six months which comes to Rs.6,500/-x 6=Rs.39,000/-.
As per the medical bills provided by the claimants, he had spent Rs.6,25,196/-.The Tribunal
without assigning any reason reduced the same to Rs.4,00,000/- which is unsustainable.
The medical evidence shows that he underwent three surgeries and was on follow-up treatment for a long time.
Therefore, the Tribunal ought to have accepted the bills produced for medical expenses of Rs.6,25,196/- and awarded the compensation on that head accordingly.
19. Having regard to the period of hospitalisation, nature of injures and period of treatment, the compensation awarded on the head of pain and suffering is on the lower - 10 - side.
The Tribunal should have awarded the compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- on the head of pain and suffering.
20. The claimant was aged hardly 26 years, a married person and having three months old baby at the time of accident.
Considering that aspect and the nature of injuries and the treatment, he must have lost lot of comforts in life at least for a period of one year.

Therefore, on the head of loss of amenities, the Tribunal should have awarded the compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-.
21.
The claimant was from Hale Thaggahalli village, Maddur Taluk, he was treated as inpatient in Mysure hospital for 88 days.
He must have spent some amount for transportation, attendant charges, food and nourishment during the period of hospitalisation.
Therefore, the Tribunal should have awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/- on the head of transportation, attendant charges, food and nourishment.
The compensation awarded on the head of future medical expenses does not warrant any interference.

22. For the aforesaid reasons the just compensation payable is as follows:

2 . Medical expenses and 6,25,196/-
 Attendant charges, Special  Diet, etc  3. Loss of income during laid 39,000/-
 up period  4. Pain and suffering 2,00,000/-

Hence, the following:
ORDER
The appeal is partly allowed.

The impugned award is modified as follows:
(i) The claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.13,00,916/- with interest thereon at 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
(ii) Respondent No.2 shall deposit the said amount before the Tribunal (on adjusting compensation already - 12 - deposited if any) within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
(iii) The award of the Tribunal with regard to apportionment and investment is maintained.
